item.title: [New] Windows 365 User settings (local admin, reset/restore, restore points, disaster recovery) go legacy in mid-November and read-only in early December 2026; auto-migration moves to April-June 2027
item.description:
Local administrator rights on Cloud PCs move to a new policy type; a recreated policy with the wrong assignment or rank can widen or drop local admin, and auto-migrated policies land at the lowest priority.

Intune · Inventory User settings policies and their assignments, recreate Enable local admin and recovery settings in Cloud PC configurations / Windows App settings, check rank, and delete the legacy policy once validated.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] November and December 2026 security updates need a restart on hotpatch-enabled Windows Server 2022; next hotpatch expected February 2027
item.description:
Hotpatch-enrolled Server 2022 hosts (often domain controllers and other tier-0 servers kept on hotpatch to avoid reboots) stay unpatched until they restart; three consecutive restart months need maintenance windows or the November fixes sit installed-but-pending.

Windows Server · Schedule restarts for hotpatch-enabled Windows Server 2022 devices for the November and December updates, and track pending-restart state in compliance reports.

item.title: [New] Eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys compromised: Windows blocked the CAs on 20 October, an out-of-band update removes seven eMudhra roots on 26 October and Edge follows on 27 October
item.description:
A certificate that chains to a compromised CA can impersonate a TLS endpoint or sign code that Windows trusts; disconnected or WSUS-only devices that never received the 20 October Disallowed list still trust it.

Windows · Make sure the Disallowed CTL and the 26 October out-of-band update reach devices without automatic root updates (offline, WSUS-only, Azure images); inventory certificates chaining to the seven removed roots and replace them before they stop validating.

item.title: [New] Out-of-band security updates for .NET, ASP.NET Core, PowerShell 7.4/7.6 and Visual Studio: the October Scan Cab was reissued on 25 October, so offline compliance scans run before then miss them
item.description:
Two remote code execution fixes outside Patch Tuesday land in runtimes that sit on web servers and admin hosts (ASP.NET Core, PowerShell 7). An offline or WSUS-scan-cab compliance report taken with the earlier cab shows these hosts as compliant while they are not.

Windows · Redeploy the reissued wsusscn2.cab wherever offline scans are used, then find hosts running .NET 8/9/10, ASP.NET Core, PowerShell 7.4/7.6 or Visual Studio in Defender Vulnerability Management and patch internet-facing ASP.NET Core servers first.
